summary: Ispaghula husk (psyllium) is a bulk-forming laxative derived from the seed coat of Plantago ovata. Its highly hydrophilic mucilage absorbs water in the gut, increasing faecal mass and softening stool to promote peristalsis. It is an over-the-counter fibre used for constipation, to regulate bowel function (IBS, diverticular disease, stoma, haemorrhoids, anal fissure) and as an adjunct that can modestly improve cholesterol and glycaemic control. It must always be taken with plenty of fluid to avoid oesophageal or intestinal obstruction.

moa: The arabinoxylan mucilage of the seed coat is highly hydrophilic and largely non-fermented. It absorbs water in the intestinal lumen to form a viscous gel, increasing stool bulk and water content. The enlarged, softened faecal mass distends the bowel wall and stimulates peristalsis, easing defaecation. The viscous gel can also bind bile acids and slow carbohydrate absorption, contributing to modest cholesterol- and glucose-lowering effects.

missed: If you miss a dose, take it when you remember, then continue as usual - it does not need to be doubled. As a regularly used fibre, consistent daily intake with adequate fluid gives the best effect.
overdose: Excessive intake may cause abdominal discomfort, marked flatulence, bloating and, if fluid intake is inadequate, faecal impaction or bowel/oesophageal obstruction. Management is supportive: increase fluid intake, withhold further doses, and seek medical care if there is severe pain, vomiting or signs of obstruction.
